canonical.name: The page works over both real and complex scalars, with the complex case changing only the absolute-homogeneity convention.
The reverse triangle inequality makes the norm $1$-Lipschitz.
Linear isometries are separated from surjective isometric isomorphisms before the completion universal property is stated.
A normed subspace is a linear subspace equipped with the restricted norm.
A complete normed subspace is closed in the ambient normed space.
A closed subspace of a Banach space is Banach under the restricted norm.
Vector addition and scalar multiplication are continuous in the norm topology.
In the published Cauchy-class model of completion, termwise operations and the limiting norm are representative-independent.
The published metric completion carries a unique compatible Banach-space structure extending the dense original copy.

contents.name: Corollary 1.2.7, finite-dimensional subspaces are closed
contents.reason: This is a genuine finite-dimensional consequence, and the design places all norm-equivalence, compact-unit-ball, and finite-dimensional closedness results on FA-3 rather than mixing them into the foundational Banach page.

contents.reason: The quotient construction is not load-bearing on FA-1 once product norms and completion are handled locally. FA-2 is the first page that needs the quotient norm, quotient completeness, and quotient universal property as primary content.

contents.reason: This theorem belongs with the quotient-space package on FA-2. Importing it here would pull quotient notation and factorization machinery onto a page whose completion block is otherwise self-contained.
